source.title: Intrinsic Guardrails: How Semantic Geometry of Personality Interacts with Emergent Misalignment in LLMs
source.authors: Krishak Aneja; Manasvi M. Mittal; Anmol Goel; P. Kumaraguru; V. Bonagiri

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The paper cites the original refusal-direction study as related work but does not test its refusal direction or refusal behavior. Its interventions use personality vectors to study emergent misalignment, a different outcome.
record.gate_note: The paper reports effects of ablating and amplifying personality and valence vectors on emergent-misalignment rates. Those rates do not measure refusal to harmful requests or refusal of harmless requests, so they do not test any listed claim version. Appendix prompts and evaluator instructions are not results.
record.test_reason: The paper cites Arditi et al. (2024) only in related work. Its interventions use persona and valence vectors built from difference-in-means of trait system prompts. The outcome is the emergent-misalignment rate on free-form Betley et al. questions, not refusal of harmful requests. No refusal direction is extracted, ablated or added, and refusal is not measured. The judge's REFUSAL category is never reported as a result.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that personality-space geometry is preserved through EM fine-tuning. Evil and SVV directions act as 'intrinsic guardrails': ablation raises EM above 40% and amplification suppresses it to under 3%. Base-model vectors transfer zero-shot to regulate EM fine-tunes.
record.recipe_differences: Uses difference-in-means vectors for prompted personality traits, then projection scaling at selected middle layers to measure EM misalignment; it does not extract a harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction or test refusal. No weight edit.
record.method_sensitivity: Effects vary by vector and model: native Evil amplification increases misalignment slightly in Llama-3.1-8B but suppresses it in Qwen models; SVV amplification reduces it in all three. Intervention layer also varies in sweeps; Layer 16 is selected for primary causal experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Projection ablation of Evil or SVV vectors raises emergent-misalignment rates in bad-medical-advice fine-tunes (e.g. +43.3% Evil and +33.8% SVV in Qwen-2.5-14B). Amplification lowers the rates, except Evil amplification in Llama-3.1-8B (+0.8%). Vectors taken from the instruct model transfer to the EM fine-tune: 32.9% on ablation and 2.1% on amplification, against a 12.5% baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Personality-valence directions causally gate emergent misalignment in fine-tuned models, and base-model vectors transfer zero-shot to the corrupted fine-tunes.

fits_no_version.finding: In the aligned Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct model, ablating Evil or SVV raises misalignment only from 0% to 3.33% and 1.25%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How much valence-vector ablation matters for misalignment depends on the model's fine-tuning (EM) state.

record.problems: The intervention evaluation uses 24 prompts with 10 generations per run and an LLM judge; the authors acknowledge possible evaluator and prompt-generation bias. The reported safety metric is a categorical EM rate, not a refusal measure. The text does not establish general capability preservation. Some intervention values are presented only in figures, and uncertainty is generally given as standard-error bars without exact values.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports additional personality-vector and principal-component intervention bars in Figures 4–5 and geometric similarity/alignment metrics in Tables 1–2 and Appendix D. These were not extracted because they concern other vectors or geometric preservation rather than refusal behavior, and the key EM intervention outcomes and model-dependent cases are represented above.

untested.parts: No harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction; no refusal removal or induction; no capability check.
No jailbreaks or adversarial training against ablation.
Multiple persona directions and PCs are compared for emergent misalignment, not for refusal.
Harm judgment is not separated from the refusal decision.
Vectors are transferred from instruct models to EM fine-tunes, but these are persona or valence vectors, not the refusal direction.

record.verdict_notes: Figure 6 also gives native and transferred SVV values that were not extracted; they are irrelevant to the refusal versions. The introduction wrongly says EM is reduced 'to near zero when ablated'. The results show this happens on amplification. The Llama -Evil value is unclear from the garbled Figure 5; Appendix C.2 gives 9.58% at layer 16.

versions.untested_parts: No refusal direction derived from harmful-minus-harmless instructions is tested; refusal removal, harmless-request refusal, and general capability are not measured.
No weight-edit or abliteration procedure is tested for refusal.
No jailbreak attack or training against ablation is tested.
The study compares personality and valence vectors for emergent misalignment, not alternative accounts of refusal directionality.
The study does not separate harmfulness judgment from a refusal decision.
Base-model vectors are transferred to EM fine-tunes, but this is not a test of transfer of the refusal direction or refusal behavior.
The study does not vary refusal training or test whether its timing or method determines a removable refusal direction.
